questions.question: Name the four changes of state and give an everyday example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Melting, for example an ice lolly melting in the sun. Evaporating, for example washing drying on the line. Condensing, for example drops forming on a cold glass or pot lid. Freezing or solidifying, for example water turning to ice in the freezer or candle wax hardening.

questions.question: Give three raw materials and the manufactured materials made from them.
questions.expected_answer: Any three, for example: sand to glass, clay to ceramics, oil and coal to plastic, wood to paper, wool to fabric, hide to leather.

questions.question: Explain two ways to make paper stronger and why triangles make frames strong.
questions.expected_answer: Any two of: folding it into a concertina, rolling it into tubes, gluing layers together, corrugating it, or making it into a hollow pillar. Triangles make frames strong because a triangle cannot change shape unless one of its sides changes length, while a square can be pushed into a diamond.
